# About Me

I am a physicist and graduate researcher at Stony Brook University studying the
quark-gluon plasma created in high-energy nuclear collisions. My research focuses on
collective phenomena and event-by-event fluctuations, with the goal of understanding how
the initial geometry of a nuclear collision and the transport properties of the resulting
medium are encoded in experimentally measurable momentum correlations.

I am a member of both the **ATLAS Collaboration** at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at
CERN and the **STAR Collaboration** at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC) at
Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL). My research combines experimental measurements
with hydrodynamic calculations and initial-state models to study the connection between
collision geometry, fluctuations, and the dynamical response of the quark-gluon plasma.

## Research

A central theme of my current work is the study of **radial-flow fluctuations**. These
measurements provide a complementary perspective on collective dynamics and offer new
ways to probe the transport properties of the quark-gluon plasma, including its bulk
viscosity.

I am also interested in nuclear structure, initial-state fluctuations, system-size
dependence, and the emergence of collective behavior across different collision systems.
